value.rationale: A sharp species-resolved relaxation rate is a natural observable in three-type heredity dynamics beyond scalar stability. The complete feasible parameter classification shows one marginal converging at n^{-1} instead of n^{-1/2} precisely when c:d=2:5 or 5:2, with the same signed coefficient -20/63 for every off-critical initial state. This counterintuitive selective speedup is a structural effect of asymmetric inheritance, not just a generic parabolic flip exponent; it can guide comparisons of relaxation observed at individual population types. General scalar flip asymptotics are explicitly treated as established background.
